review_scope: Reviewed all 23 main/candidate frame pairs and checked the toaster, upper kitchen and watch station at full size. Rendered brightness differences are retained in the packet. Mesh and material inventories match at the targeted stations and the composed technical surface contract passes. The ordinary dialogue frame was reviewed separately.

images.observation: The floorboard, mantel and tabletop textures remain readable. Both captures retain the spiral floor detail and the companion framing.
The wall tile and grout stay readable where the flashlight crosses the curtain edge. The brass companion trim and toilet seat remain distinct.
The resident, blind slats, radiator fins and timber floor remain legible. The right-hand highlight is present in both images.
The ceiling lamp and window slats retain their outlines. A warmer cast on the near furniture leaves the floorboards and shelf finish readable.
The fixed cabinets, counters and worn plaster stay visible, with a rounder, more concentrated flashlight patch in the candidate. The 17 surveyed matching meshes and material bindings are identical.
The face, valve fittings and copper runs remain outlined against the dim service room. The boiler still meets the floor at the same edge.
The bookcase, bentwood chair and closet leaf remain framed as in main. The timber finish reads through a modest exposure shift.
The tile grid and metal strip retain their clean edges. Tile value shifts slightly around the tank, with the corner and exposed fasteners still distinct.
The fixture view remains very dark in both frames. The brick face and horizontal mortar stay discernible.
The fuse seats, open leaf and conduit stay legible. The wall and shadow levels differ visibly while the 34 matched mesh and material records are identical.
The counter rail, tile and shadowed pet silhouette remain in the same under-counter view. The brass strip still reads against the darker wood.
The orange cat and pale forepaws are visible on the cabinet beside the framed picture. Contrast remains low in both images.
The ceiling support, two frames and cabinet top remain readable. The inherited standing view offers little close detail of Lafitte.
The metal mail faces and slot labels remain legible above the bench under the existing dim light.
The cast-iron fins, towel and blind slats remain readable. Subtle room-light variation leaves the radiator and skirting edges intact.
The safety cage, railings, door frame and lighting conduit retain their separation. The warm landing still reads through both images.
The water tank profile and metal banding remain visible against the city and sky. The roof parapet trim retains its material definition.
The candidate shows stronger cool highlights on the terminal. Its housing, display and frame geometry remain recognizable and all 10 matched mesh and material records are identical.
The tiled corner, cistern and exposed metal edges remain legible through the close camera angle.
The residue still reads against the floorboards and chair under the lamp. Both images retain the distinctive colored shape and shadow boundary.
The upright strands remain distinct from the radiator and floor. The same material response remains visible around the lit base.

The candidate renders the toaster and tins brighter and more silver. The toaster tray, crumbs and adjacent worktop remain readable, and all 29 matching toaster mesh and material bindings are identical.
The faceplate, brass fitting and wall texture remain legible at full size. Shadow levels differ while all 38 watch-station mesh and material records match.
